title: Keep tool attribution across a steering preempt
body:
Keeps tool-call attribution and foreground subagent spawns alive across a steering preempt, so a tool still running when the user steers is completed and rendered rather than left at Running forever.

## Defect

When a steering message preempts a running Claude turn, the SDK emits a `result` for the preempted turn even though the protocol turn is not over. The pipeline already treats that as an intermediate result and defers `ChatTurnComplete` until the queue is drained. The mapper did not: `mapResult` cleared the `tool_use_id` attribution map and drained foreground subagent spawns on every `result`, intermediate ones included. A tool call still in flight when the steer landed lost its attribution, so its later `tool_result` hit the unknown-id path and produced no `ChatToolCallComplete`. The tool stayed Running indefinitely, and any subagent it had spawned vanished from the registry, so `subagent_started` was never emitted and the inner signals were buffered forever.

## Fix

Turn-end cleanup belongs to the component that knows when the protocol turn ends. `mapResult` now maps usage and error signals only. The router exposes `clearPendingTurnState`, and the pipeline calls it in the same branch that fires `ChatTurnComplete`, so attribution is dropped exactly once, on the final result. Abort and dispose paths are unchanged in practice: no `result` is routed after an abort, and stale entries are still dropped on the next turn's final result with the existing orphan warnings.

## Tests

Mapper:
- `result keeps a pending tool_use so a tool_result that lands after a steering preempt still completes it`
- `result keeps a foreground subagent spawn in the registry`
- `clearPendingToolCalls drains tool_use entries that never received a tool_result and warns once per orphan`

Pipeline, driven through the real queue and router:
- `intermediate result during steering keeps tool-call attribution so a later tool_result still completes the tool`
- `intermediate result during steering keeps the foreground subagent spawn so inner content still announces subagent_started`
- `final result drops pending tool-call attribution so a late tool_result is treated as unknown`

The first two in each group fail without the fix and pass with it. Sibling suites (pipeline, router, tool-call registry, subagent registry and signals, prompt queue, replay mapper) all pass. No new type errors.

title: Accept remote workspace folders in working-directory actions
body:
Lets a session in a remote window add, remove and replace working directories without the reducer throwing, by validating the same set of schemes on the create path and the action path.

## Defect

`resolveSessionWorkingDirectoryAction` threw `Working directory must be a file URI` for any non-`file:` directory. The client dispatches raw workspace-folder URIs, which in a dev container are `vscode-remote://dev-container+...`, so every dynamic multi-root add, remove or replace from a container window threw. Meanwhile `createSession` accepted and stored those same URIs with no scheme check at all. The reducer asserted an invariant the creation path never enforced.

## Why not normalize to `file:` at ingress

Host state is echoed back verbatim and compared against the window's `vscode-remote:` folders: the session list uses `isEqualOrParent(directory, folder.uri)` and the working-directory synchronizer diffs `state.workingDirectories` against `folder.uri` and dispatches the raw folder URI. A `file:` entry would never match, so the session would drop out of the list and the synchronizer would re-add the folder on every reconcile. Host state already holds `vscode-remote:` working directories by design: `sessionPermissions` has a test for a non-`file:` working directory, several host features branch on the scheme and degrade, and providers take the cwd via `fsPath`, which yields the path either way.

## Fix

One predicate, `isSupportedWorkingDirectory`, accepts `file:` and `vscode-remote:`. Both throw sites in the reducer use it, and `createSession` now validates its `workingDirectories` with the same predicate before any side effect, so the two paths cannot drift apart again. Genuinely unsupported schemes (`untitled:`, `https:`, `vscode-vfs:`) are still rejected on both.

## Tests

- `accepts and canonicalizes vscode-remote set, remove and replace actions`
- `accepts exactly the schemes isSupportedWorkingDirectory accepts`
- `rejects malformed and unsupported URIs` and `rejects a replace with an unsupported replacement URI` (updated)
- `applies vscode-remote working-directory actions to a session created with remote folders`
- `validates working-directory schemes the same way as working-directory actions`

`sessionWorkingDirectories.test`: 17 passing. `agentService.test`: 407 passing, 0 failing. No new type errors.

## Out of scope

`_hostAddressableWorkingDirectories` in the session handler filters create-time folders by the host's default-directory scheme, which can drop `vscode-remote:` folders before create on one path. That is a separate defect on the client side and is not changed here.

title: agent host: restore channel state after a host restart
body:
Fixes an agent host crash leaving sessions rendering a running turn forever.

## Symptom

Two Codex sessions in the Agents window showed a running spinner for an hour. The Codex `app-server` was idle at 0% CPU the whole time — both turns had already aborted. Only the client's view was stale.

## Root cause

The agent host utility process died of a V8 OOM (heap 3.67 GB) and was auto-restarted 1 ms later. Recovery then failed in two independent places.

Timeline from the AHP wire log:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| `11:40:58` | Agent host OOMs. Both Codex rollouts record `turn_aborted` at this second. |
| `+1 ms` | `AgentHostProcessManager` restarts it. |
| `11:41:03.232` | `reconnect` → `-32008 NotFound`. Correct: the client registry is in-memory, and this is a new process. |
| `11:41:03.233` | Client falls back to `initialize` with its 35 current subscriptions → `serverSeq: 22`, **13 snapshots**. Only root, automations and `*/annotations`. No session or chat channels. |
| `11:41:03.237` | `authenticate` for `https://mcp.eng.ms` → `-32007`. |
| `11:41:03.255` | Client disconnects — the rejection propagated out of `Promise.all` and the catch disposed the transport. |
| `11:41:05.258` | `reconnect` with `lastSeenServerSeq: 22` → **`type: "replay"`**, 146 envelopes (seq 23–389). |
| → +1 h | Session and chat channels never re-subscribed. Stale `activeTurn` persists. |

### Defect 1 — one rejected credential aborted the whole recovery

`_restoreAuthenticationAfterFreshInitialize` pushed every cached authentication through a single `Promise.all`. `_authentication` accumulates arbitrary per-resource credentials, so one MCP server the restarted host no longer recognised rejected the entire batch. In `_attemptReconnect` that skipped `_restoreSubscriptionsAfterFreshInitialize` entirely.

The `-32007` itself is correct behaviour: codex only accepts an MCP token once it can map the resource to a configured server (`codexAgent.ts` `handleAuthenticationToken`), and the spec requires rejecting resources the host does not currently advertise.

### Defect 2 — the server offered a replay to channels with no baseline

`_addInitialSubscription` registers a state channel even when its snapshot is absent — it calls the **synchronous** `_stateManager.getSnapshot`, unlike `_subscribeStateChannel`, which awaits `AgentService.subscribe` and restores evicted session state. Its own doc comment says so: *"Valid state channels remain subscribed even when their snapshot has not materialized yet."* That is why 35 subscriptions yielded 13 snapshots.

`canReplay` then compared only the global cursor:

```ts
const canReplay = params.lastSeenServerSeq >= oldestBuffered;
```

On a freshly restarted host the replay buffer is empty, so `oldestBuffered` falls back to `serverSeq` and `22 >= 22` passes. The 146 deltas accumulated *during* the async restore. Deltas applied onto a channel with no baseline change nothing, so the pre-crash `activeTurn` survived untouched — and `activeTurn` maps directly to the UI's running state.

Neither defect alone is visible. Defect 1 skipped the re-subscribe; defect 2 ensured nothing else ever supplied the missing state.

## Not provider-specific

The affected paths are the shared AHP layer. `protocolServerHandler.ts` reconnect logic contains zero provider references, and the reproduction test added here uses a `copilot:` session URI.

The same `initialize` in this incident returned `/annotations` for the `copilotcli:` sessions but likewise no session or chat channels — three Copilot sessions were equally stranded. They went unnoticed only because they were idle: a stale *idle* is indistinguishable from a fresh one, whereas a stale *running* is not.

Provider-level healing does not rescue this. Codex maps an interrupted turn to `Cancelled` and Copilot attaches `interruptedTurnError`, but both are host-side and reach the client only inside a snapshot — `_ensureDefaultChat` seeds restored turns in place rather than dispatching actions, precisely because it expects a later `subscribe` to carry them.

## The fix

### Client — `agentHostProtocolClient.ts`

- **Tolerate a rejected cached credential.** Only the freshly resolved *initial* authentication is fatal; other per-resource tokens are logged and stepped over. Connection-closed errors still rethrow.
- **`_subscriptionsAwaitingRestore`.** Records channels a fresh initialize did not snapshot, and drains them. Entries deliberately survive a transport drop, so a later reconnect finishes the job even when it resolves to a snapshot-less `replay`. The set is rebuilt on each fresh initialize and reconciled against later snapshot/`missing` results.
- **`_authenticationRestorePending`.** Carries an interrupted authentication pass to the next reconnect. Scoped deliberately: authentication is process-global and survives a transport drop, so only a frame that never reached the host needs redelivery — ordinary replays do not re-authenticate. Matters most for cloud sandboxes, whose sealed-token resolver is not optional.

### Subscriptions — `agentSubscription.ts`

- **`beginSnapshotRefresh()` / `cancelSnapshotRefresh()`.** Buffers envelopes while a re-subscribe is in flight. These channels are already live server-side, so an action newer than the snapshot can arrive first; previously `handleSnapshot` would clobber it, since existing buffering only applies before the *first* snapshot (`_confirmedState === undefined`). Losing the action that ends a turn would recreate the original symptom.

### Server — `protocolServerHandler.ts`

- **`_baselineDebt`.** Per-client set of state channels handed out without a snapshot. `canReplay` is denied while any requested channel still owes one, forcing a snapshot response.
- Debt is released when a baseline is delivered, when a channel is reported `missing`, and on unsubscribe. That last part matters: `_hasBaselineDebt` uses `.some()`, so an unreleasable entry would deny replay for *all* of a client's channels permanently. This incident's reconnect reported 15 dead terminal channels, so it would have triggered in production.

This is the half that protects non-VS Code consumers: the AHP repo ships six client SDKs, and the TypeScript and Swift runtimes preserve subscriptions across a fallback initialize without re-subscribing the channels it omitted.

## Deliberately not changed

Two further concerns were investigated and rejected rather than fixed:

- **Retrying a rejected MCP credential.** Already self-heals — `_autoAuthenticateMcpServer` re-authenticates non-interactively when codex surfaces `McpServerStatus.AuthRequired`, which is exactly when the resource→server mapping exists. Retrying earlier would also contradict the spec requirement to reject unadvertised resources.
- **A deadline on reconnect requests.** There genuinely is none, but session restoration legitimately takes ~48 s for large catalogs, and closing the client does not cancel host-side restoration — later attempts join the same pending promise. A timeout would manufacture failures without healing anything.

## Testing

`6175 passing, 0 failing` across `**/platform/agentHost/test/**`. Hygiene, `valid-layers-check` and `typecheck-client` clean.

Each fix has a test verified to fail without it:

| Test | Without the fix |
|---|---|
| `reconnect answers replay even when initialize gave a channel no baseline` (server, real `ProtocolServerHandler`) | `reconnectType: 'replay'` |
| `a channel reported missing does not deny replay for the client's other channels` | second reconnect stuck on `snapshot` |
| `restores subscriptions when a cached resource authentication is rejected after a host restart` | no `subscribe` issued at all |
| `finishes an interrupted post-restart subscription restore on the next reconnect` | replay-path transport never re-subscribes |
| `finishes an interrupted authentication restore on the next reconnect` | zero `authenticate` frames on the replay path |
| `keeps an action that arrives before the post-restart restore snapshot` | `stillActive: 'turn-1'` — the original symptom |
| `snapshot refresh buffers newer envelopes...` (+ cancel path) | newer envelope discarded |

The server reproduction needs the buffer empty at reconnect so `oldestBuffered` falls back to `serverSeq`, with deltas accruing during the async restore — matching the incident. A first attempt that generated the actions beforehand filled the buffer, made `canReplay` false, and did **not** reproduce.

## Not addressed

The OOM itself. The agent host reaching 3.67 GB needs a separate memory investigation; this PR only ensures a crash recovers cleanly instead of stranding sessions.

title: Settle the promise of a pending request the remote reconcile dropped
body:
Fixes the settlement loop in `syncPendingRequestsFromRemote` so a pending request the host dropped has its promise settled on the client.

## Defect

`syncPendingRequestsFromRemote` captured `existing` as `model.getPendingRequests()`, which returns the model's live `_pendingRequests` array. `replacePendingRequests` then empties and refills that same array in place, so the loop meant to settle every request the remote reconcile removed iterated the replacement set instead. Every id in that set is in `reconciledIds`, so nothing was ever settled. A queued or steering request the host consumed or discarded kept its promise pending on the client indefinitely. Every other caller in the tree snapshots the array first; this one did not.

## Fix

Snapshot the array before replacing it.

## Test

`syncPendingRequestsFromRemote settles the deferred of a request the remote dropped`: two queued requests, a remote set containing only the first; the dropped one settles as rejected with the removal reason while the kept one stays pending. The test fails without the fix (97 passing, 1 failing) and passes with it (98 passing, 0 failing).

Part of #333174.

title: Scope chat mouse-back interception to the chat widget
body:
Mouse back/forward stopped navigating editor history in 1.135.0. Regression from #331126 (`c178d46`), which registered a **capture-phase** `mousedown` listener on the entire workbench container and consumed button 3 whenever the chat widget merely held focus — including clicks over the editor.

## Root cause

`HistoryService.registerMouseNavigationListener()` implements `workbench.editor.mouseBackForwardToNavigate` with a **bubble-phase** listener on `layoutService.mainContainer`. `ChatViewPane` attaches a capture-phase listener to the same container and calls `EventHelper.stop(event, true)` + `stopImmediatePropagation()`, so history navigation never runs.

The handler's only spatial scoping was `document.activeElement` being inside the chat widget, but pressing a mouse navigation button does not move focus — and the chat input auto-focuses. Forward appeared broken too because the forward stack is only populated by a successful Back.

## Changes

- **`chatViewPane.ts`** — require the `mousedown` to originate inside the chat widget before consuming it. This strictly narrows the existing condition; the `activeElement` check is retained, and the global capture listener still wins the race against `HistoryService` for clicks within the chat view.

  ```ts
  if (!isAncestor(event.target as HTMLElement, this._widget.domNode)) {
      return;
  }
  ```

- **`historyService.test.ts`** — added coverage for the previously untested feature: dispatches real `mousedown` events with buttons 3/4 and asserts the active editor changes and the event is consumed. `createServices` gained an optional `mouseBackForwardToNavigate` flag since `HistoryService` reads that setting at construction time.

title: Allow dragging a grouped session back into its workspace section
body:
## Description

Once a session was moved into a custom group in the Agents window sessions list, it could not be dragged back out: `SessionsListDragAndDrop` had resolvers for pinning, adding to a group and reordering, but none for leaving a group. Dropping a grouped session on its workspace section fell through to the reorder path, where `canReorderOnto` rejects drops whose dragged sessions don't share the target's group membership.

### Changes

- **New drop target** — `resolveRemoveFromGroupTarget` runs in `onDragOver` and `drop`, ordered after the add-to-group resolver and before plain reordering. It accepts the `workspace:` section header (drop *over*) and the sessions rendered in that section (drop *before*/*after*), producing the same highlight/insertion feedback as the add-to-group path.
- **Scoped acceptance** — the drop resolves only when every dragged session is currently in a custom group *and* belongs to that same section, so unrelated workspace sections and their sessions keep rejecting it.
- **Single source of truth for section membership** — `SessionsList.getWorkspaceSectionIdOfSession` mirrors `groupByWorkspace`'s id (`workspace:<label>`) and returns `undefined` under date grouping and for pinned, done and quick-chat sessions, which render elsewhere:

  ```ts
  const dragged = this.draggedSessions(data);
  const canRemove = dragged.every(session =>
      this.delegate.getGroupIdOfSession(session) !== undefined
      && this.delegate.getWorkspaceSectionIdOfSession(session) === sectionId);
  ```

- **Drop handling** — `removeSessionsFromGroup` clears membership through `ISessionGroupsService.removeFromGroup` (the same call the "Remove from Group" context-menu action uses, so default placement won't re-add the session) and then reorders the sessions into the dropped slot when the drop landed on a session.

The shared harness now records `applySortChanges` so reordering can be asserted. Both accepting tests were confirmed to fail without the production change.

### Known gap

When a grouped session is the only session of its workspace, that workspace section is not rendered at all (grouped sessions are excluded from sectioning), so there is no drop target and the context-menu action remains the way out. Rendering empty workspace sections would also have to change the "more workspaces" capping logic, so it is left out of this change.

title: Allow closing a session's main chat tab
body:
Closes #333988

The session's main chat could never be closed. This replaces that rule with a single invariant:

> A session always keeps at least one visible chat tab.

Any chat including the main one can now be closed, except the last remaining visible tab. Closing only **hides** a chat — it stays reopenable from the Chats picker and "Reopen Last Closed Chat", and is never deleted (the main chat still reports `canDelete: false`). <kbd>⌘W</kbd> now behaves like a browser: it closes the active tab, and falls through to closing the session on the last one.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6a9af0a-fd73-4662-a30c-9a783e3f6cce

### Also included

While a lone **non-main** chat was on screen, the header showed the *session* title, so nothing identified which chat you were looking at. The tab strip now also appears when the single visible tab isn't the main chat.

### Implementation notes

- `_closedChatUris` stays the raw persisted intent; a new `_effectiveClosedChatUris` resolves it for display — the active chat is never hidden, and the main chat is forced open if the closed set would otherwise hide every chat.
- `CloseAllChatsAction` now opens the main chat before closing the rest, so it remains the survivor of the batch.
- The close-chat keybinding and the tab's close button are gated on the chat being a visible tab that isn't the last one.

title: fix(chat): preserve #file reference when editing text before it
body:
Fixes #333941

Editing text before an inline `#file:` reference (for example, pressing
Backspace immediately before it or retyping an earlier word) could delete
the reference entirely.

The existing recovery logic handled replacements that enclosed the reference,
but did not preserve the reference when unrelated edits changed its offset.
Such edits could therefore fall through to the removal path.

This adds a `touchesReference` check to distinguish edits that overlap the
reference from edits that occur outside it. For non-overlapping edits, the
reference range is recomputed from the net offset delta instead of removing
the reference. Edits that touch the reference continue to remove it.

Added regression tests covering deletion before the reference, replacement
before it, deletion touching its first character, and edits both before and
after the reference in a single change event.

Manually verified the behavior with a real `#file:` reference in a running
dev build.

## How to test

1. Open Chat.
2. Type a sentence, e.g. `Compare the ownership section of `.
3. Type `#`, pick a file so `#file:README.md` is inserted inline, then continue typing `with the current draft.`
4. Move the caret before the reference and edit there — e.g. press Backspace immediately before it, or retype a word right in front of it.
5. Confirm the `#file:README.md` reference is preserved instead of being deleted.

Also covered by the added tests in `chatVariables.test.ts` (delete-before, replace-before, delete-touching-first-char, edits-before-and-after).

title: terminal: cancel unnecessary telemetry timeout on disposal
body: Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/276610 ### Details When a terminal is created, terminal telemetry waits for the process to become ready and then allows another 10 seconds for shell integration. If the terminal is closed during that delay, telemetry is sent immediately, but the unused timeout continues until it expires. The timeout is bounded to 10 seconds, so this is not a permanent memory leak. Repeatedly creating and closing terminals can still leave several unnecessary timeout promises pending at once. ### Change Cancel the shell integration timeout when the per-terminal telemetry listeners are disposed. ### Before When creating and closing a terminal 37 times, pending terminal telemetry promises remain until their 10-second timeouts expire: ### After The timeout is canceled when the terminal closes, so the pending promise settles immediately. ### Test Video [terminal-create.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14982627-fcfa-4e55-a002-e1b815262a6c)

</details>

title: automations: fix: exclude archived sessions from unread badge
body:
## Context

The Automations entry in the left sidebar derives a single status from automation runs. After needs-input and in-progress runs, a completed or failed run contributes an unread indicator when its linked session is unread.

Archived sessions can intentionally retain their unread state. Previously, the status derivation did not consider archive state, so an archived unread session kept the Automations entry marked as unread.

## Fix

Require a terminal automation session to be both unread and not archived before it contributes the unread indicator.

The archive check uses the existing observable reader, so the UI reacts immediately when a session is archived or restored. Archiving does not mutate the session's unread state, and restoring an unread session makes it eligible for the indicator again.

Needs-input and in-progress status precedence is unchanged. The accessible “unread run” label follows the same corrected derived status.

## Test coverage

Extended the focused `SessionSectionRenderer` test to verify:

- completed and failed unread runs still produce the unread status;
- archiving removes the status;
- restoring brings the status back;
- unread state remains unchanged; and
- equivalent session URIs continue to match correctly.

The test factory now exposes its settable archive observable in its return type, avoiding a type assertion.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --grep "SessionSectionRenderer"` — 4 passing
- `git diff --check`

title: Agent Host: Manage idle Dev Container lifecycle
body:
## Summary

Stop session-owned Dev Containers after all of their sessions become idle, restart them on demand for later work, and remove them before archiving their mounted worktrees.

Tracking issue: #317380

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Stop at host idleness**: A container is stopped only after every session on its provider has left active or input-needed state, and no unsent draft remains.
- **Retain the provider**: Stopping withdraws the runtime connection but preserves the dynamic provider and cached sessions so a later send can restart the container and reconnect transparently.
- **Suppress automatic resurrection**: The shared process records a stopped workspace and rejects automatic relay reconnects. Only an explicit user operation can resume it, and suspension clears only after a successful connection.
- **Remove before worktree cleanup**: Archive waits for the host to accept the archived state, removes the container, and only then archives/removes the mounted worktree.
- **Preserve shared consumers**: Archiving one session does not remove a container while another unarchived session or unsent draft still uses that provider.
- **Keep local paths authoritative**: The existing opaque worktree handle remains the remote metadata boundary; container operations use the locally retained source/worktree URI.

</details>

## Changes

- Add shared-process operations for stopping and force-removing the known container for a workspace.
- Serialize container connect, stop, and remove operations and disconnect all relays before Docker lifecycle commands.
- Preserve stopped state across failed resumes and block background reconnects from other windows.
- Keep the runtime provider registered while stopped and reconnect it before subsequent sends or archive operations.
- Stop after all sessions become idle, while preserving active sessions and unsent drafts.
- Confirm archive actions through a retained session subscription before container/worktree teardown.
- Recreate the worktree before starting the replacement container on unarchive.
- Add cross-process coverage for Docker operations, reconnect suppression, failures, drafts, shared sessions, and rejected archives.

## Validation

- 337 affected unit tests passing, 11 pending
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files
- Repository pre-commit hygiene
- `git diff --check`

A full live Dev Container run from `main` remains blocked by the independent AHP version mismatch between `main` (0.9) and the currently published Insiders CLI (provisional 1.0).

title: Update proxy agent to 0.45.0
body:
## Summary

Update `@vscode/proxy-agent` to `0.45.0` in the root and remote dependency manifests.

This version loads Node.js system certificates in a worker on macOS and starts loading during proxy resolver creation, preventing slow keychain trust evaluation from blocking the extension-host main thread.

Fixes #333830.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run hygiene`
- Root and remote dependency trees resolve to the published `@vscode/proxy-agent@0.45.0` tarball.
- Confirmed the published package contains `out/systemCertificatesWorker.js`.
- Confirmed system certificates load through the worker and it exits successfully.
- Product Build 470171 successfully packaged the worker into the macOS application's `node_modules.asar`. All non-macOS stages passed; macOS failures occurred later in ESRP signing and universal notice comparison.
